case_name: Girdhari Lal vs. Smt.Anita @ Kamli & Anr.
facts_of_case: Petitioner filed an application under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act for grant of divorce on the ground of cruelty against respondent. The case was fixed for re-conciliation but failed. Petitioner's statement has been recorded and now case is fixed for his cross-examination.

legal_principles.principle: Every petition under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 should be tried as expeditiously as possible and endeavour shall be made to conclude the trial within six months from the date of service of notice of the petition on the respondent.
legal_principles.held: From the above referred provisions of the Act, it is clear that every petition under the provisions of the Act is to be taken on day to day basis and endeavour has to be made to conclude the trial within six months

legal_principles.principle: The trial of a petition under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 should be continued from day to day until its conclusion unless the court finds the adjournment of the trial beyond the following day to be necessary for reasons to be recorded.
legal_principles.held: It is provided that trial of the petition under this Section shall be continued from day to day until its conclusion unless the court finds the adjournment of the trial beyond the following day to be necessary for reasons to be recorded

outcome.final_order: The Family Court No.2, Jaipur was directed to conclude and decide the application within a period of three months.

use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act
responding to a writ petition in a family court
advising on matrimonial disputes and reconciliation
